subject: best way to upload larger datafiles

messages.author: 66aaf5d139ba9c7f
messages.subject: best way to upload larger datafiles
parts:
I am trying to determine the most efficient way to load data into a shiny-app. I put an example that simulates data (20K rows and 100 variables) on Github as a gist (https://gist.github.com/4527821
). The file that is generated is about 15MB and loads into Rstudio very fast as you would expect. When using fileInput in shiny it takes quit a bit longer and when I use options(shiny.trace=TRUE) I see lots of 'iterations' (see example output below). 

Is this something in my code? Is it due to the fact that fileInput is still experimental? Should I be using file.choose(), lazyloading, ...?

Note that I am mainly interested in allowing users to load larg(er) datafiles into a locally running shiny-app.

RECV $$binary data$$
SEND {

"value": null 
}

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: best way to upload larger datafiles
parts: I think file.choose() is the answer for now, until we can beef up fileInput. Even calling it "experimental" is a little generous; the current implementation is little more than a proof of concept.
